images.title: Rows of 8 stay rows of 8
images.purpose: Shows 16 as 2 rows of 8 and 56 as 7 rows of 8 stacked into 9 rows of 8, so 16 + 56 = 72 = 8 × 9.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One dot grid of 9 rows in the centre with three short labels on the right.
images.exact_structure: A grid of 9 rows of 8 dots, 72 dots in all, evenly spaced. The top 2 rows (16 dots) are teal (#0072B2) and carry a brace on the right labelled 16 = 8 × 2. The lower 7 rows (56 dots) are amber (#E69F00) and carry a brace on the right labelled 56 = 8 × 7. A tall reddish purple (#CC79A7) brace on the left spans all 9 rows, labelled 72 = 8 × 9. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Joining multiples of 8 gives a multiple of 8, because the rows of 8 just stack up.

image_decisions.why: Stacked rows of 8 show at once why a sum of multiples of 8 is a multiple of 8.
